examples.question: Reference: RFI 107 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 1 HSS Column Clash with Existing Truss Clarification MAS Metals RFI 004 Attached Markup and Pictures 1/A4.1.1 and 2/S2.01 call out the new HSS4X4 colum to be conceal in the wall near GL5&J. Per post-demo investigations, it was observed that there is an existing truss above this wall which will clash with the new HSS column. Please advise if it is acceptable to shift the column outside of the wall per sketch in red to avoid clashing. The new column would be wrapped in an encased gyp. column. Please confirm.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): M. Tye - See attached with ASK-24. Per comments on attached, no structural exceptions, architectural finish and HSS column concealment in ASK-24.

Impact: The clash prevents the installation of the new HSS column as designed, requiring a shift of the column outside of the wall.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct thorough post-demolition investigations to identify existing structural elements before finalizing design.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 21 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Flooring Removal in Existing Conference Room 02H6C Confirmation Sheet AD2.1.2 and Note D21 in sheet AD2.1.2 Existing Conference Room 02H6C is to become the new employee Breakroom which will be getting new LVT plank flooring. root_causes: Existing carpet in Conference Room 02H6C is not indicated for removal in the demo plans.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 28 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Wood Doors Finish Confirmation Submittal 081000-1 - Doors, Frames and Hardware Attached Pictures Per Forge/Abbott comment on DFH Submittal, new wood doors are to follow the called out existing doors as BOD. The callout on the door schedule is stating a PS Cherry door. Additionally, existing BOD doors are stained in a custom color that does not match any stock options. There are schedule and cost

examples.question: Reference: RFI 109 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Janitor's Room FRP Confirmation A2.1.2 Per building code, mop sinks typically have FRP installed at the adjacent walls. examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): M. Tye, see attached RFP panel specification and location at 2nd Floor Janitors Mop Sink.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 2 - Abbott Alameda HBP - Fire Rated Walls and FSDs Confirmation Sheets M-1.2 and M-1.3 Attached Marked Up Picture Fire Smoke Damper (FSD) locations are not called out on the Mechanical Drawings. examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi: Please see attached PDF.

examples.prevention_action: Ensure all fire-rated wall details and FSD locations are clearly indicated in the mechanical drawings during the design phase.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 103 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 1 Wood Veneer Clarifications Detail 9/A9.6.0 Sheet A7.1.0 No elevation or layout is provided for the wood veneer paneling called out in detail 9/A9.6.0. 1) Please provide elevation showing the extent of the veneer installation (i.e. full height or partial height installation). 2) Additionally, please provide a layout that should be followed (ie panels to be installed vertically or horizontally).
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): REFER TO ATTACH FOR COMMENTS. 10/30/25 - ASK-22 UPDATED. SUPERSEDING PREVIOUS VERSION. 11/17/25 EY: ASK-22 UPDATED, ISSUING ASK-22.2 SUPERSEDING PREVIOUS VERSIONS ISSUED PRIOR. ASK22.2 SUPERSEDES RFI #106 RESPONSE ISSUED ON 10/30/25.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 103.1 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 1 Wood Veneer Panel Wall Framing Clarifications DPR submitted RFI 103 to clarify the design intent for the wood veneer panels that are to be installed at Stair 1. As a result, Tipping Engineers provided the response below for the framing / backing / blocking requirements at this wall. However, after analyzing the information provided, DPR concluded that it would be much cheaper and easier to demo the existing wall and build a new wall with 16GA studs. Per the meeting held on 11/04/2025 with Forge, Tipping, and DPR, please confirm it is acceptable to demo and re- build the existing wall adjacent to Stair 1. Please provide all structural and architectural details for the framing at this location.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): FORGE 11/11/25 EY: FORGE DOES NOT ANTICIPATE ANY ARCHITECTURAL CHANGES SUBJECT TO STRUCTURAL'S REVISION.
root_causes: Framing/backing/blocking requirements for wood veneer panels at Stair 1 were unclear, leading to the conclusion that existing wall should be demoed and rebuilt.
Impact: Increased costs and additional work required to demo and rebuild the wall instead of following the original framing plan.
examples.prevention_action: Provide detailed framing and blocking requirements in the design documents to avoid ambiguity.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 41 - Abbott - Alameda 1420 HBP - Floor Drains in Men's Restrooms Relocation Clarification UMI RFI 001 Attached Sheet A4.4.0 Mark Up Attached Sheets P1.1 and P1.2 Mark Up Architectural drawing A4.4.0 shows a wall addition at the urinal location for Men’s Restroom 02C8B and 0218A. Plumbing drawing P1.1 shows no wall addition and P1.2 shows a smaller wall addition than the Architectural drawings. This wall addition will conflict with the existing floor drain layout in the Men’s restrooms and will require the floor drains to be relocated under the new Partition as shown in the attached A4.4.0 markup. Please advise if the floor drains are to be relocated as shown in the markup or if the added wall is to not get installed to maintain original drain location. Please note if the shown added wall is not installed, there will be a larger space at the urinal location.
examples.resolution: Marieca Tye: New partitions at the men's urinals can be removed from scope, please see additional comment regarding accessible clear space at urinal on the attached RFI response
root_causes: Architectural drawing A4.4.0 shows a wall addition at the urinal location for Men’s Restroom 02C8B and 0218A, while plumbing drawings P1.1 and P1.2 show conflicting wall additions.
Impact: The wall addition will conflict with the existing floor drain layout in the Men’s restrooms, requiring the floor drains to be relocated.
examples.prevention_action: Improve coordination between architectural and plumbing design teams to ensure alignment of drawings before finalization.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 55 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Grease Duct Framing Clarification ASK-13 R1 Sheet A2.1.2 Detail 2/S5.01 Attached Pictures Per detail 2 on ASK-13 R1, a new wide flange beam is being called out. examples.question: Reference: RFI 60.1 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Elevator Vestibule Door 01D9C Height Confirmation Sheet A0.1.0 (Dated 11/08/2024) Sheet A0.1.0 (Dated 03/06/2025) Elevator Vestibule Door 01D9C was originally called out to be 7'-0". When the DFH submittal for this door was submitted, it was approved to be a 7'-0". At some point during the permit revision drawings, the door was changed from 7' to 8'-10 1/2" height door. This change was never clouded or communicated to DPR. Since this was not captured during submittal, the door frame and door got ordered to be 7'-0". The framers installed framing for a 8-10" door. In order to avoid delaying the project, please confirm DPR is to proceed with adjusting the framing to accept the 7'-0" door as originally approved.
examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi (FORGE - 10049724): Please see attached PDF.
root_causes: Elevator Vestibule Door 01D9C was changed from 7'-0" to 8'-10 1/2" height in permit revision drawings without communication to DPR.
Impact: Framing was installed for an 8'-10" door, but the ordered door and frame were for a 7'-0" door, leading to a need for adjustment.
examples.prevention_action: Implement a communication protocol for changes in permit revision drawings to ensure all parties are informed.

examples.question: In keeping with the level 3 electrical room wall finish and to prevent re-opening walls to install backing for controls, security, and telecom panels intended to be installed in ER 245 that do not have final installation location coordinated at this time, DPR proposes installation of fire rated plywood on all ER 245 walls. Suggested answer Corgan, please confirm it is acceptable to install fire rated plywood at all ER 245 walls to support wall mounted equipment attachment. If so, Corgan, please confirm plywood to be painted with PT-1 and the height above RAF the plywood is to be installed to.
examples.resolution: Ashley Hill (Corgan - 10059759): CONFIRMED, FIRE RATED PLYWOOD IS ACCEPTABLE. CONFIRMED, TO BE PAINTED PT-1. HEIGHT OF PANEL TO BE COORDINATED WITH HEIGHT OF EQUIPMENT. SS/WR - CORGAN - 9.5.2025
root_causes: Final installation locations for controls, security, and telecom panels in ER 245 were not coordinated at the time of wall finish installation.
Impact: Requires additional work to install fire rated plywood on all ER 245 walls to support wall mounted equipment attachment, preventing the need to reopen walls later.
examples.prevention_action: Coordinate final installation locations for all equipment prior to wall finish installation.

examples.question: There are door hardware requirement discrepancies between the phase 3 security drawings issued by PSG and the current Architectural drawings. See referenced attachment for latest security drawing issuance by PSG with rough-in markups proposed via RFI 78.1. The security drawings call for access control security power supply to support access control devices and electrified hardware at new door 224 and existing doors 229, 271, and 272. All of these doors do not have a power supply or electrified hardware per their respective spec'd hardware schedule or DFH submittal. Door 229 does not currently have any access control devices, however, doors 271 and 272 do. DPR requests clarification if door 224's hardware schedule is to be updated to include power supply and electrified hardware for security. Additionally, if existing doors 229, 271, and 272 are to be modified to support added security deployment. Conversely, doors 231B and 262 call for power supply and electrified hardware per the contract documents, but there is no access control shown at these doors per the security drawings. DPR requests clarifications if the door 231B and 262 hardware schedules are to be updated. Suggested answer PSG/Corgan, please clarify if hardware schedules for doors 224, 229, 271, 272, 231B, or 262 are to be updated to support the access control design per the latest security drawings.
examples.resolution: steven holt: Door hardware is not in the security Scope of Work. Please have the door company verify. Only request we have is that all door hardware have a request to exit device built into it.
root_causes: Discrepancies between phase 3 security drawings and current Architectural drawings regarding door hardware requirements for doors 224, 229, 271, and 272.
Impact: Potential modification of existing doors and updates to hardware schedules to support access control security deployment.
examples.prevention_action: Implement a thorough review process for hardware specifications across all related drawings before finalizing designs.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 70 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Low Wall Framing Confirmation Email Confirmation from SEOR Markup Sheets A7.00, A9.5.0, and S6.01 This is a confirming RFI to document that the low wall shown in detail 6/A9.5.0 is to be constructed out of metal stud framing and not wood framing. examples.question: Reference: RFI 47 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Restrooms Existing Conditions Confirmations Attached Pictures with Markups Sheet A4.4.0 Drawing sheet A4.4.0 provides design intent for the 2nd floor restrooms. DPR was contracted to only provide new finishes in these restrooms. However, additional work needs to be completed due to the existing conditions of the framing. Question 1: Existing framing only goes to 8' height. RCP calls for 9' ceilings. Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to proceed with 9' ceilings. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 2: Plumbing will need to be removed to install the new 3 5/8" studs (@ 10' tall for the 9' ceilings) and re- installed after framing is complete. Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to with removal and re-install of plumbing due to new framing installation. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 3: Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to proceed with shifting of plumbing carriers plan north to accommodate the ADA stall layout. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 4: Concrete wall calls for paint. Imperfections will be very noticeable if the wall is only primed and painted. Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to proceed with adding hat channels and drywall at this location to create a finished surface. Furred wall will have a total thickness of 1-1/2" off concrete wall. Please confirm no exceptions.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu: Work is approved with no exceptions, see attached for additional comments.
root_causes: Existing framing only goes to 8' height while RCP calls for 9' ceilings.
Impact: Requires removal and re-installation of plumbing to accommodate new 10' tall studs for the 9' ceilings.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct thorough existing conditions survey prior to finalizing design and scope.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 60.1 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Elevator Vestibule Door 01D9C Height Confirmation Sheet A0.1.0 (Dated 11/08/2024) Sheet A0.1.0 (Dated 03/06/2025) Elevator Vestibule Door 01D9C was originally called out to be 7'-0". When the DFH submittal for this door was submitted, it was approved to be a 7'-0". At some point during the permit revision drawings, the door was changed from 7' to 8'-10 1/2" height door. This change was never clouded or communicated to DPR. Since this was not captured during submittal, the door frame and door got ordered to be 7'-0". The framers installed framing for a 8-10" door. In order to avoid delaying the project, please confirm DPR is to proceed with adjusting the framing to accept the 7'-0" door as originally approved.
examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi (FORGE - 10049724): Please see attached PDF.
root_causes: Elevator Vestibule Door 01D9C was changed from 7'-0" to 8'-10 1/2" height in permit revision drawings without communication to DPR.
Impact: Framing was installed for an 8'-10" door, but the ordered door and frame were for a 7'-0" door, leading to a need for adjustment.
examples.prevention_action: Implement a communication protocol for changes in permit revision drawings to ensure all parties are informed.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 69 - Phase 1B Restrooms Existing Conditions Modifications Confirmation Detail 1/A4.4.0 Attached Pictures with Markups Similar to the restrooms in Phase 1A, the only scope of work was to add new finishes to the walls, floors, ceilings, and installation of new plumbing fixtures, partitions, and counters. However, after doing the initial demolition, DPR noticed that the same issues were being observed in the Phase 1B restrooms. Please see the attached pictures and confirm if the proposed modifications are acceptable. Question 1: Concrete wall calls for paint (once tile is removed). Imperfections will be very noticeable if the wall is only primed and painted. DPR proceeded with adding hat channels and drywall at this location to create a finished surface. Furred wall will have a total thickness of 1-1/2" off concrete wall. Please confirm no exceptions taken to doing the same for restrooms in Phase 1B. Question 2: Similar to the restrooms in Phase 1A, please confirm DPR is to proceed with providing new plumbing carriers at the wet walls. These carriers will need to be relocated once installed to accommodate the ADA stall layout. Question 3: Existing framing only goes to 8' height. RCP calls for 9' ceilings. Please confirm no exceptions for DPR to proceed with re-framing walls to accommodate the 9' ceilings. Question 4: Existing transfer duct in the restrooms, neither do the demo plans nor do the mechanical plans mention a transfer duct within this space. Please confirm if transfer air ducts are to stay in place. Please also confirm if new ceiling grille (similar to CEF-1) is required for the transfer air ducts. Question 5: Similar to Phase 1A restrooms, plumbing will need to be removed to install the new 3 5/8" studs (@ 10' tall for the 9' ceilings) and re-installed after framing is complete. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 7: Per CBF, electrical receptacles in men's and women's restrooms (Phase 1B) will need be upgraded as the current circuits are not code compliant. The existing feeds do not have ground, and the existing conductors are undersized. New home runs will need to be pulled back to the panel. Panel B circuits 3 and 5 are being utilized. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 8: Existing electrical conduit is currently sitting on top of the 8' ceiling framing. Please confirm it is acceptable to remove the conduit and replace it with flex where needed and provide proper supports per code.
examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi (FORGE - 10049724): Please see attached PDF.
root_causes: Existing framing only goes to 8' height while RCP calls for 9' ceilings.
Impact: Requires re-framing of walls to accommodate the 9' ceilings, leading to additional labor and material costs.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct a thorough review of existing conditions and verify framing heights during pre-construction surveys.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 28 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Wood Doors Finish Confirmation Submittal 081000-1 - Doors, Frames and Hardware Attached Pictures Per Forge/Abbott comment on DFH Submittal, new wood doors are to follow the called out existing doors as BOD. These doors are a Rift White Oak door. However, this is in conflict the existing doors surrounding the construction area and with the callout on the door schedule of the same submittal (4th page). The callout on the door schedule is stating a PS Cherry door. Additionally, existing BOD doors are stained in a custom color that does not match any stock options. There are schedule and cost
examples.resolution: Marieca Tye: 1. Rift White Oak per submittal and confirmed in OAC on 2/18/25 2. Confirmed to proceed with custom Stain See attached for full comments
root_causes: The door schedule calls for a PS Cherry door, while the existing doors in the construction area are Rift White Oak, creating a conflict.

Impact: The discrepancy between the specified door type and the existing doors necessitated additional work to confirm the use of Rift White Oak and to create a custom stain that matches the existing custom color.
examples.prevention_action: Ensure thorough review of existing conditions against door schedule during design phase

examples.question: Reference: RFI 35.1 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Header Detail at (N) Stairs 2 Doors Clarification DFH Submittal - Door Schedule RFI 35 Response ASK-07 Markup Attached Pictures (N) Stair #2 Double Doors were added per RFI 35. New pair of doors are to be 7'-0" tall. Existing doors are 8'-10" tall. Details provided in ASK-07 only show door framing details. Question: Please provide header framing detail to bring the opening framing to the correct height.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): -EY 04/08/25 PROVIDE GYP HEADER AS NEEDED FOR DOOR FRAME.
root_causes: Existing door height is 8'-10" while new doors are specified to be 7'-0" tall, requiring adjustment to the header framing.
Impact: Requires additional framing work to accommodate the new door height, potentially delaying the project and increasing costs.
examples.prevention_action: Ensure complete door framing details are included in the initial design documents.

examples.question: There are door hardware requirement discrepancies between the phase 3 security drawings issued by PSG and the current Architectural drawings. See referenced attachment for latest security drawing issuance by PSG with rough-in markups proposed via RFI 78.1. The security drawings call for access control security power supply to support access control devices and electrified hardware at new door 224 and existing doors 229, 271, and 272. All of these doors do not have a power supply or electrified hardware per their respective spec'd hardware schedule or DFH submittal. Door 229 does not currently have any access control devices, however, doors 271 and 272 do. DPR requests clarification if door 224's hardware schedule is to be updated to include power supply and electrified hardware for security. Additionally, if existing doors 229, 271, and 272 are to be modified to support added security deployment. Conversely, doors 231B and 262 call for power supply and electrified hardware per the contract documents, but there is no access control shown at these doors per the security drawings. DPR requests clarifications if the door 231B and 262 hardware schedules are to be updated. Suggested answer PSG/Corgan, please clarify if hardware schedules for doors 224, 229, 271, 272, 231B, or 262 are to be updated to support the access control design per the latest security drawings.
examples.resolution: steven holt: Door hardware is not in the security Scope of Work. Please have the door company verify. Only request we have is that all door hardware have a request to exit device built into it.
root_causes: Discrepancies between phase 3 security drawings and current Architectural drawings regarding door hardware requirements for doors 224, 229, 271, and 272.
Impact: Potential modification of existing doors and updates to hardware schedules to support access control security deployment.
examples.prevention_action: Implement a thorough review process for hardware specifications across all related drawings before finalizing designs.

examples.question: Per 10/17 discussion between DPR and PSG, each double door between UPS room should have a sounder mounted above the door header. The current security drawings do not reflect this. Suggested answer PSG, please confirm if the UPS room double doors, 241B, 242B, 243B, 246C, will require sounder devices. If so, please provide updated security drawings reflecting this update.
examples.resolution: steven holt: Attached is the ED typical for a contact and sounder double door only Latest revision attached as deiscussed.
root_causes: Security drawings do not reflect the requirement for sounder devices above the double doors in the UPS room.
Impact: Additional work and cost incurred to update security drawings and install sounder devices above the specified double doors.
examples.prevention_action: Ensure all security requirements are included in the initial drawing set and verify with stakeholders before finalizing designs.
